title: Refs and DOM Core Check
description: Check your understanding of refs, useRef, DOM access, ref forwarding, and imperative handles.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is a ref commonly used for?

options.text: Storing a mutable value or accessing a DOM node without causing renders

questions.explanation: Refs hold mutable values across renders and can point to DOM nodes.

questions.prompt: Updating ref.current triggers a component re-render.
questions.explanation: Refs are mutable containers; changing current does not notify React or trigger rendering.

questions.prompt: When is it safe to access a DOM node assigned to a ref?

options.text: After React has committed it, such as in an effect or event handler
While creating JSX during render for layout reads

questions.explanation: DOM refs are set after commit and are commonly used in effects or event handlers.

questions.prompt: Which are good ref use cases? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: Refs are useful for imperative DOM work and mutable values that do not affect rendered output.

options.text: A component to receive a ref from its parent and pass it to a child or DOM node
A child to mutate parent props

questions.explanation: forwardRef lets a component participate in the ref chain.

options.text: The value exposed to a parent through a ref
The dependency array of useEffect only

questions.explanation: useImperativeHandle can expose a small imperative API instead of a raw DOM node.

questions.prompt: Refs should generally be avoided for normal React data flow that affects what appears on screen.
questions.explanation: State and props are the normal way to drive rendered output.

questions.prompt: If a ref may not be attached yet, what should code usually do before using ref.current?
questions.explanation: Safe DOM access accounts for null before mount, after unmount, or conditional rendering.
